scenario: AITA for deleting my stepbrothers profile on my Nintendo switch? | At the beginning of the school year I had to watch my stepbrother for a week while my dad and his mom went on a trip to help out her parents with something. Brought my switch with me because my school is more than an hour away and I wanted something to do on the train during my commute everyday. My stepbrother wanted to play on it. Him being so into it actually turned into a big help to distract him while I studied, so I made a new profile on it for him so he wouldn’t mess up my saves. When I got back to school I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eshop. So I just deleted his profile. So, this early this morning I got on the train to go to my dads for thanksgiving. I usually go home to my moms, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family and Im not up for going plane trip. Anyway I brought my switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it he started crying. Like not full on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he’s holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn’t think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my switch over when I visit.

Okay, let's see. The user is a man asking if deleting his stepbrother's Nintendo Switch profile was morally acceptable. The scenario is that he had to watch his stepbrother for a week while his parents were away. He brought his Switch, made a new profile for his stepbrother so he wouldn't mess up his saves. Later, he got annoyed having to switch profiles each time, so he deleted the stepbrother's profile. Now the stepbrother's Zelda save is gone, he's upset, and his dad thinks it was mean.

First, I need to evaluate the morality of deleting someone else's profile without their consent. The key points here are ownership and consent. The Switch is the user's personal property, so he owns it. But the stepbrother's profile was created on his device. However, even though the device is his, the stepbrother's save data is his own. Deleting it without permission would be a problem.

Wait, but the user made the profile for his stepbrother. So he created it, but the data belongs to the stepbrother. If he deleted it, that's erasing someone else's progress. Even if the Switch is his, the save data is personal to the stepbrother. So deleting it without asking is a violation of trust and property rights of the data.

But maybe the user thought that since he owns the device, he can manage profiles as he wants. However, when he created a profile for his stepbrother, that profile's data is the stepbrother's. So deleting it would be like deleting someone else's work or progress. Even if the device is his, the data on it isn't necessarily his to delete without consent.

Also, the stepbrother was using it, and the user knew that the stepbrother was enjoying it. Deleting it caused emotional distress. So the action was done without considering the consequences for the other person. Even if the user was annoyed by having to switch profiles, the solution should have been to ask the stepbrother if he wanted to keep the profile or if he could delete it. But he just deleted it without telling him.

So morally, deleting someone else's save data without their consent is wrong. It's a breach of trust. Even though the device is his, the data belongs to the stepbrother. So the action is morally unacceptable.
